walkthroughs.body_html:
Graphic Communication — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Graphic Communication brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Graphic Communication.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which designer is famed for using negative space in mid-twentieth-century film posters?
options: Paul Rand
Saul Bass
Milton Glaser
David Carson

mcqs.q: Which colour model is standard for full-colour print production?
options: RGB
CMYK
HSL
LAB
A whole typeface that looks formal.
The small projecting line at the end of letter strokes.
Using exactly three colours.
The space between letters.

mcqs.q: What is the rule of thirds?
options: A strict mathematical rule that must never be broken.
Using exactly three colours.
A guideline placing key elements along lines or intersections of a 3x3 grid.
Photographic accuracy.

mcqs.q: What were Impressionist painters primarily trying to capture?
options: The fleeting effects of light and atmosphere at a particular moment.
Using exactly three colours.
Photographic accuracy.
Their feelings or first impressions of a scene.
